intent: Link to the previous page of a paged result set with a chevron and a short label.
typical_uses: The previous link at the start of the page row
Half of a previous/next pair with no page numbers

dont_use_when.situation: A link to one numbered page
A link to the next page

invariants.text: The link renders a left chevron before the label and ignores children. Its accessible name is the fixed `aria-label` "Go to previous page", set ahead of the consumer's props: `text` changes only the visible label, and only an `aria-label` passed to it replaces the name.
The visible label is hidden below a 640px viewport width (pagination.module.css `.previousNextText`), so a narrow viewport shows the chevron alone.

anti_patterns.do_instead: Pass a matching `aria-label` with a custom `text`, so the visible label stays part of the accessible name

a11y.by: pagination.test.tsx asserts getByRole('link', { name: 'Go to previous page' }) finds the link, with the visible "Previous" label and an svg inside it

rtl.by: pagination.tsx renders ChevronLeftIcon in the link and pagination.module.css has no rule that mirrors it under a right-to-left direction, so in a right-to-left row it points against the reading order

unexposed_parts.reason: pagination.tsx renders a ChevronLeftIcon inside the link; it is not exported as a component of its own and cannot be replaced.
pagination.tsx renders `text` in a span with the stylesheet's previousNextText class; it is not exported, and `text` is the only control over it.

good.title: A custom label with a matching accessible name
good.code: <PaginationPrevious href="?page=1" text="Newer" aria-label="Go to newer results" />

bad.title: A label given as children
bad.why: The link renders fixed content and ignores children; the visible label is set through `text`.
